name: MNIST Database of Handwritten Digits
description: The MNIST database of handwritten digits has a training set of 60,000 examples and a test set of 10,000 examples. It is a subset of a larger set available from NIST, with digits size-normalized and centered in fixed-size 28x28 grayscale images.

publisher.name: Yann LeCun & Corinna Cortes (Courant Institute / Google Labs)

license.name: License not established from original source
license.notes: The original publisher page was unavailable during this review. A standard license or commercial-use grant was not established. Terms from mirrors are not assumed to cover the original distribution.

source_references.notes: Canonical hosting page maintained by Yann LeCun.

source_references.notes: Foundational 1998 paper introducing LeNet-5 and benchmark results on MNIST.

source_references.title: NIST Biometric Database Catalog: MNIST
source_references.notes: Corroborates 60,000 training and 10,000 test examples; does not establish a dataset license.

verification.notes: 2026-10-29 scoped review: NIST corroborates the training/test counts, but the original MNIST source could not be retrieved. Original license evidence remains unresolved. Raw data files were not downloaded or inspected.

size.notes: Sum of four compressed IDX gzip archive files.

citation.paper_title: Gradient-Based Learning Applied to Document Recognition

provenance.collection_method: Constructed from NIST Special Database 3 (high school students) and Special Database 1 (Census Bureau employees).
provenance.curation_notes: Normalized to fit in a 20x20 pixel box while preserving aspect ratio, centered in a 28x28 field by computing the center of mass.
